Payment in full is required for all tracts; Contract for deed is not an option for this 2026 land auction. *** SEE RESOLUTION, TERMS AND CONDITIONS, AND CITY OF FINLAYSON LETTER, REGARDING TRACT 1, WHICH DID NOT SELL AT THE SEPTEMBER 18, 2026 AUCTION *** Signage is posted at Tract 1 2026 Pine County Tax-Forfeit Land Courthouse Auction Entire Packet RESOLUTION 2026-30, Terms and Conditions, and Listing Tract 1 Available over-the-counter at EMV (see resolution, terms and conditions above) City of Finlayson letter regarding Tract 1's ordinance violation(s) Tract 2 Sold $1,006 (EMV) on 9-18-2026 Tract 3 Sold $16,000 on 9-18-2026 City of Sturgeon Lake letter regarding Tract 3's ordinance violation(s) | GENERAL INFORMATION FOR ALL LAND AUCTIONS Please contact the Pine County Land Department at 320-216-4226 if you have questions after viewing the following information. All tracts are sold "as-is" and must be purchased at or above the indicated value for that tract (EMV, appraised value, minimum bid, etc). Contract for deed will be a payment option for some tracts, whereas payment in full will be required for other tracts. This is determined based on date of forfeiture and state statute. See terms and conditions of individual land auctions. Interest Rates on Contract For Deed Purchases Potential buyers are encouraged to thoroughly research properties and check with local planning and zoning authorities. Information on searching land records (Landshark) can be found on the Pine County Recorder Office website . Parcels can also be searched for on the Pine County Beacon website . Official plats with lot dimensions and other details can be found here , and may have useful information on some of the land auction tracts. Landlocked Property Info: Landlocked land does not have legal access. We do not recommend anyone purchase landlocked land without legal access. However, for those interested in landlocked land, you can contact and arrange access with adjacent land owners. If cooperative access cannot be obtained, please be aware that Minnesota State Statute 164.08 offers specific direction on gaining access through cartway law. All cartway proceedings are unique to the situation. Be aware that typical cartway process may involve legal expenses, purchase of the cartway and/or other fees paid to the land owner, survey costs, construction costs, etc. The local township is actively involved in the cartway process.
